subject.title: Feature: Add denylist support for exec-approvals

question: What native exec-approvals denylist policy shape should OpenClaw support for command/content matches under permissive exec policies?
rationale: The request changes persisted security/config behavior across core runtime, gateway protocol, node host, UI, CLI/docs, and open PRs propose different semantics that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Review the direct denylist PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/92456 as the main candidate and require protocol, prompt-parity, docs, upgrade, and live behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Land path-deny first
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88075 as a narrower sensitive-path hardening track while keeping command/content denylist policy open.

options.title: Reject native denylist mode
options.body: Close the denylist direction only if maintainers decide allow-everything-except policies are outside OpenClaw's security model and should remain plugin or external policy-engine territory.

recommendation.title: Review the direct denylist PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/92456 as the main candidate and require protocol, prompt-parity, docs, upgrade, and live behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete provided the latest maintainer-facing review and has the strongest current history signal on the exec approvals policy surface.
